record.paper_title: Open problems in queueing theory inspired by datacenter computing
record.original_question: In the limited fork-join model, what is the mean job response time when each arriving job dispatches its k tasks to the k shortest queues, or to the k queues with the least work, rather than to random queues?

evidence.quote: Analyzing the case where the k tasks are dispatched to the k shortest queues, or k queues with least work is also an interesting open problem

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the following limited fork–join queueing model. There are N identical first-come-first-served servers, each with its own infinite-capacity queue and unit service rate. Jobs arrive according to a Poisson process of rate λN (so that the per-server arrival rate is λ < 1). Each arriving job consists of exactly k ≤ N tasks. The task service times are i.i.d. exponential with mean 1 (or, in a second variant, i.i.d. from a general distribution G with finite mean). A job is considered complete only when all k of its tasks have finished service; its response time is the time from arrival until the last of its k tasks completes.

In the standard limited fork–join model the k tasks of each arriving job are dispatched to k servers chosen uniformly at random (without replacement) from the N servers. Consider instead the following two dispatch policies:

(a) Join-the-k-Shortest-Queues (JSQ-k): upon arrival, the job sends its k tasks to the k servers whose queues currently contain the fewest tasks (ties broken arbitrarily).

(b) Join-the-k-Least-Work (JLW-k): upon arrival, the job sends its k tasks to the k servers with the smallest remaining workload (sum of remaining service requirements of all tasks currently at that server).

Determine, in closed form or via a tractable analytical expression, the mean job response time E[T] in steady state under each of policies (a) and (b), as a function of N, k, λ, and the service-time distribution.
artifact.status_search_result: A literature search on fork-join queueing analysis (including the ACM Computing Surveys survey on fork/join systems and works on JSQ routing) reveals analyses of random-dispatch limited fork–join queues and of JSQ for single-task jobs, but no closed-form or tractable analytical expression for the mean response time when each arriving job dispatches its k tasks to the k shortest queues or to the k queues with the least work. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Analysis of Fork/Join and Related Queueing Systems
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of fork-join queueing analyses; treats random dispatch and approximations but does not give exact mean response time for k-shortest-queue or least-work dispatch.
status_evidence.claim: No exact analysis for k-shortest / k-least-work dispatch in limited fork-join is reported in the standard survey.

status_evidence.title: Analysis of join-the-shortest-queue routing for web server farms
status_evidence.snippet: Analyzes JSQ routing for single-task jobs in server farms.
status_evidence.claim: JSQ analyses in the literature focus on single-task jobs, not on fork-join jobs splitting into k tasks routed to k shortest queues.

status_evidence.title: Fork–join queue - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Overview of known exact and approximate results for fork-join queues.
status_evidence.claim: Standard reference summaries do not include exact mean response time for k-shortest-queue dispatch in limited fork-join.
